label: copy-phase input m (fed-back orig token 1-3)
explanation: Token detector for m that only fires in the copy phase, when m is fed back in as an input. It is strongest when the m is original token 1 (recall_idx 2; top examples are near max 3.9) and weaker for original tokens 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4). It is almost silent when m is original token 0 (recall_idx 1, rate 0.3%) or token 4 and later. It never fires on m in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token. It does not depend on the output token or the previous token. Activations on later and repeated m inputs are weak.

issues: Systematic false-positive class the explanation never mentions: on the final copy step (to_go == 0) the feature is almost always off. On dev, predicate & (to_go == 0) gives 5598 predicted steps with precision 0.024 and 0.03% of activation mass. These come from short sequences, where original token 1-3 is the last token fed back, e.g. 'v x m w <DEL> v x *m*' and 'd o o m i <DEL> d o o *m*'. They are the bulk of the original predicate's ~7k test false positives.
Adding (to_go >= 1) raises dev F1 from ~0.90 to 0.956 and precision from 0.85 to 0.96 while keeping mass recall at 0.995. Test: precision 0.963, recall 0.951, F1 0.957.

The other claims check out. Activity is zero in the original and delimiter phases, all activation mass is on in_tok m, recall_idx 2 carries the most mass (0.545) and the top examples, recall_idx 1 fires at a rate of 0.3%, recall_idx 5+ is about 0, and the feature does not depend on out_tok or prev_tok.

The false positives left after the fix look minor: some second occurrences of m inside the copy window (e.g. 'f v m m k e'), and some recall_idx 3-4 m's in long sequences that stay inactive. The misses left are weak recall_idx 1 m activations (about 0.5% of mass).
